newsitem.title: USA: Ariz. Four Corners 220 MW unit 3 restart uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Ariz. Four Corners 220 MW unit 3 restart uncertain.

text.p: Restart of the 220 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Four Corners coal-fired plant in New Mexico is uncertain following the discovery of contamination in its boiler, a spokesman for Arizona Public Service Co said Tuesday.
The unit was shut November 8 due to a boiler tube leak, but the outage was extended for cleaning of the boiler and turbine system.
The boiler water system now needs to be flushed and a timeframe for restart is uncertain, the APS spokesman said.
Four Corners also has two 740 MW units and two 170 MW units.
Arizona Public Service, a subsidiary of Pinnacle West Capital Corp, owns 100 percent of Four Corners units 1, 2 and 3 and holds a 15 percent stake in units 4 and 5.
